newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Albright visits Singapore for talks.
newsitem.headline: Albright visits Singapore for talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright flew into Singapore on Tuesday for a 24-hour visit aimed at bolstering an already strong trade and security relationship, officials said.
"Secretary Albright's visit will serve to further deepen the strong ties enjoyed by the two countries," a statement by the Singapore Foreign Ministry said.

"The close relationship in economic, trade and investments is reinforced by cooperation on defence and security issues as well as on political issues at the regional and international level," it added.
Albright will be holding talks with Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and Foreign Minister S. Jayakumar.

Economic and defence ties between the two nations are extensive. Singapore is the ninth largest trading partner of the U.S. It also provides logistic support and repair facilities for U.S. forces in the region.
But ties have also been ruffled by disagreements over the past few years.

The issues range from the caning of American teenager Michael Fay, which triggered a furore in the U.S., to differences on how to treat the military junta in Burma or Washington's relations with China.
